preamble: A voiceless aspirated alveolar affricate [tsʰ] replaced by a voiced unaspirated [dz]. The only documented case found is in Thebo Tibetan, where a regular voicing rule (Classical Tibetan ⟨bts-⟩ > /dz/) creates verb paradigms alternating aspirated /tsʰ/ (present, imperative) with voiced /dz/ (past); analogical leveling is now spreading /dz/ into the /tsʰ/ slots. The change is lexically restricted and not a general sound law.

examples.note: Older speakers keep /tsʰũ/; younger speakers use /dzũ/, leveling the imperative to the voiced past stem ⟨btsangs⟩ /dzɔ̃/ (Yang, Tshering & Gates 2024, Table 15 and p. 723).
Present ⟨vtshum⟩ and imperative ⟨tshums⟩ are both realized /dzʊ̃/, taking the voiced initial of the past ⟨btsums⟩ /dzʊ̃/; the authors reconstruct earlier /tsʰʊ̃/ (Table 15, Table 28).

sources: Yang, D., Tshering, S., & Gates, J. P. (2024). A voicing rule for non-continuant obstruents in Thebo Tibetan. Language and Linguistics 25(4): 710–746. https://doi.org/10.1075/lali.00169.san
